sources.entry: Wire Desktop - Standalone Electron app for the chatapp Wire.

summary.one_liner: Wire Desktop is the Electron-based standalone desktop client for the Wire chat app, wrapping the wire-webapp for macOS and Windows.
summary.what_it_does: The repository holds the source for the Wire desktop app, which wraps the wire-webapp in an Electron shell and supports macOS and Windows. Developers clone it, install dependencies with Yarn, and run it with yarn start or test it with yarn test. Build tasks produce macOS and Windows packages. The README also describes a managed-device (MDM) flag that forces App-lock on, and desktop SSO behavior: on macOS through ASWebAuthenticationSession via an optional objc-js bridge, and on Windows through an embedded SSO window with a shared persistent session. Logging to a dated electron.log file is enabled automatically. The README states that the code is part of Wire's source and includes licensing and trademark terms for building apps that connect to Wire servers.
use_cases: Build or modify the Wire desktop chat client
Run Wire desktop from source for development
Package Wire for macOS or Windows
Test single sign-on behavior in the desktop app
Study an Electron wrapper around a web app
notable: Wraps the wire-webapp in an Electron app for macOS and Windows
macOS desktop SSO uses ASWebAuthenticationSession with Safari fallback
Windows SSO uses a shared persistent session and a local text dialog for window.prompt()
MDM override flag for forcing App-lock, read from Windows registry or macOS managed preferences
Four-stage deployment flow from dev to staging to main
caveats: Supports only macOS and Windows according to the README
Requires Node.js matching .node-version and Yarn; the README also lists Git and npm as prerequisites
Disabling asar packaging via ENABLE_ASAR is noted as not recommended
Open Source Apps built from this code are subject to Wire's terms and restrictions on server connections; the Wire trademark is not licensed
